answer: An identity registers by locking a bond of 600 tokens for 40 epochs and binding to a one-per-device credential, recorded as a knoll entry. Forging N identities locks 600N tokens, of which 90 percent is slashed if attestation fails. Splitting a credential across copies adds 600 tokens of marginal cost per identity and flags the shared ivory stake for independent jurors, who vote across the bridge to trigger slashing.
